The run is finished, but the chosen chip fails the sensitivity target. On the 4 held-out synthetic patients it caught 2 of 5 seizures (0.4 against a target of 0.8). False alarms passed at 0 per hour, though over only 1.33 hours of recording, so that figure is very uncertain.

**The chip:** `band-2cmp` (lab id `c0f1ed1c57da`). It fires when signal activity is high and the amplitude-to-line-length ratio is above a threshold.
- **Size:** 86 gates, or 124 gates plus 28 flip-flops with the streaming wrapper and the 3-of-5 majority smoothing. That is well under your 300-gate limit.
- **Checks:** it matched the model bit for bit on 4,800 held-out windows and was proved equivalent. The streaming version with the same smoothing then ran 4,800 frames with no mismatches.
- **Cost:** about 650 µm² on sky130. It fits on Tiny Tapeout (sky130 or GF180) for 370 EUR.
- `estimate-cost`, `score-events` and `chip-report` all ran. I skipped layout, timing and power as you asked, so there is no power figure.

**Why it fails:** I chose it by the rule: the smallest design that clears every target on validation.
- `band-2cmp` and `band-3cmp` (143 gates) both cleared validation, and `band-2cmp` is smaller.
- On held-out data `band-3cmp` did better: 0.8 sensitivity with 0 false alarms per hour.
- The rule forbids switching on held-out results, so I kept `band-2cmp`.
- The validation set had only 4 patients and 5 seizures, so the choice rests on very few events.
- A third candidate, a simple weighted sum, came out as a constant "never fires" circuit with 0 gates.

**Changes from your brief:**
- **Harder data:** the first synthetic set was too easy, since every design was perfect on validation. I made seizures weaker, made muscle artefacts stronger and more frequent, and went to 16 patients.
- **Longer recordings:** they are 20 minutes each instead of "a few minutes", so false alarms per hour could be counted at all.
- **Scoring fix:** my own scorer counted one long always-on alarm as a single correct detection. I fixed it by splitting alarms longer than 300 seconds, as the standard SzCORE scoring does. The lab's `score-events` gave the same figures as my fixed scorer.

The next step I'd suggest is a larger validation set, which would likely pick `band-3cmp` and still stay under 300 gates. All figures are on synthetic data, not patient data.

# ChipIn report: 2-electrode seizure flag (synthetic data)

**All results here are on synthetic data, not patient data and not clinical evidence.**

## What was built
- Synthetic data: 16 simulated patients, 20 min each, 256 Hz, 2 channels, 1–2 seizures each plus muscle and
  motion artefacts (`data/assumptions.md`). Split by patient: 8 train / 4 validation / 4 held-out (`data/split.json`).
  Recordings are 20 min rather than "a few minutes" so false alarms per hour can be counted at all.
- Features (front-end, outside the chip): per channel, line length and mean amplitude over 1 s, log-quantised
  to 4 bits → chip input 4 lanes × 4 bits. One decision per second.
- The first synthetic set was too easy (every design was perfect on validation), so seizures were made weaker,
  muscle artefacts stronger and more frequent, and the number of patients went up. A scoring flaw (one long
  always-on alarm counted as a single hit) was fixed by splitting alarms longer than 300 s, as SzCORE does.
- Reference (no chip limits): float MLP with 16 hidden units. Synthetic data, validation: sensitivity 1.0, 1.5 FA/h;
  held-out: sensitivity 1.0, 0.75 FA/h.
- Candidates (all 2 channels; thresholds fitted on training patients only; 3-of-5 majority smoothing):

| Design | Lab id | Gates | Depth | Val sens | Val FA/h | Held-out sens | Held-out FA/h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lin-4lane (linear, weights −1..1) | 29455c73c45a | 0 (constant 0, never fires) | 0 | 0.0 | 0 | 0.0 | 0 |
| **band-2cmp** (activity AND amp/LL above threshold) | c0f1ed1c57da | **86** | 15 | 0.8 (4/5) | 0 | 0.4 (2/5) | 0 |
| band-3cmp (adds an upper amp/LL bound) | 5bb4789aeea2 | 143 | 18 | 1.0 (5/5) | 0 | 0.8 (4/5) | 0 |

## Choice
**Rule applied: among the designs that clear every target on validation, the smallest.** band-2cmp and
band-3cmp both clear on validation (synthetic data); band-2cmp has fewer measured gates (86 vs 143), so it was chosen.
On held-out data band-3cmp did better, but the rule forbids changing the choice using test results.
Validation had only 4 patients and 5 events, so "clears" rests on very few events.

## Targets (chosen chip, held-out synthetic data, lab `score-events`, SzCORE profile)
| Target | Value | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| Sensitivity ≥ 0.8 (primary) | 0.40 (2 of 5 events) | **fail** |
| False alarms ≤ 1 /h | 0 /h over 1.33 h | pass (wide uncertainty: only 1.33 h) |
| Under 300 gates (user's words) | 86 core gates; 124 gates + 28 flip-flops with stream wrapper and smoothing | pass |

Held-out patients meeting both targets: 1 of 4.

## Chip (from lab `chip-report` and `compile-stream`)
- Verification level 3: bit-exact on 4800 held-out windows (level 1), formal equivalence proof (abc cec, level 2),
  and streaming RTL simulation of the Tiny Tapeout wrapper with `postproc` majority 3-of-5, 4800 frames, 0 mismatches, lint clean (level 3).
  No patient recordings exist; only the synthetic held-out windows were used.
- Area (sky130, before layout): 654 µm² (174 GE). Cost: Tiny Tapeout sky130 or GF180 fits, at 370 EUR (lab `estimate-cost`; not medically certified).
- Not done: layout, timing and power (skipped on purpose to keep the run short), so there is no power or energy figure.
- Files: `chip.v` (streaming top), `*.ir.json`, `results.json`, `score_*.json`, `cost.json`, `chipreport.json`.

## Next step
Choose on a bigger validation set (more synthetic patients or real EEG, e.g. a public scalp-EEG set) so the
selection does not rest on 5 events. That would likely favour band-3cmp (143 gates, still under 300).
Then run timing-power to get a power figure at 1 decision/s.

# Synthetic data assumptions (synthetic data)
- 256 Hz, 2 channels (behind-ear bipolar pair), 16 patients x 20 minutes each (longer than "a few minutes" so FA/h can be measured at all).
- Background: pink-ish noise, per-patient amplitude 0.6-1.6x.
- Seizure: 3-7 Hz rhythmic spikes growing in amplitude, 20-60 s, 1-2 per patient, moderate (0.7-1.5x background), visible on both channels with a
  per-patient channel gain (one channel can be weak).
- Artefacts that look like events: chewing/muscle bursts (high-frequency, high line length, 2-8 s) and
  eye-blink/motion slow swings (high power, 1-3 s), 10-20 muscle and 6-12 motion per patient.
- Split by patient: 8 train, 4 validation, 4 held-out (data/split.json).

# Spec (restated from the user's spec.json; not changed)

- Device: behind-the-ear EEG patch, used at home, task: monitoring.
- Signal: EEG, 2 channels (budget: at most 2 channels for every candidate).
- Detect: seizure onset; the chip makes one yes/no decision per 1 s window (chosen: 1 decision/s).
- Targets: sensitivity >= 0.8 (primary metric), false alarms <= 1 per hour.
- Size: under 300 gates (user's words).
- Data: SYNTHETIC (user asked for simulated data). All figures are "synthetic data", never patient data.

## Choices where the spec is silent (chosen by ChipIn)
- Sampling rate 256 Hz; 1 s windows; features (line length and power per channel) computed by the analog/front-end
  and quantised to 4 bits per lane before the chip. The chip is the classifier only.
- Power budget: not given; we report the lab's estimate.

## Can each target be measured?
- Sensitivity and FA/h: yes, at the event level on held-out synthetic patients (lab `score-events`).
  A few minutes per patient give few events and little hourly exposure, so FA/h has wide uncertainty.
- Under 300 gates: yes, measured by lab synthesis.
